mechanism: state financing buys capacity, teachers, and fee relief -> more secondary places
method: two-way FE (country+year), CR1 SE clustered on country
heterogeneity_country_type: HOLDS in Asia (+0.189**, se 0.090, 19 ctys) and where 1990 secondary GER was LOW (+0.132*, 17 ctys); FAILS outside Asia (+0.010, ns) and in already-high-GER countries (+0.077* weak)
data_source: data/panel_results.csv spec S01 lag5; data/panel_heterogeneity.csv region/base_ger
literature_source: no clean causal cross-country estimate located; see LITERATURE_ELASTICITIES.md (Duflo 2001 school-construction IV is the nearest causal anchor, not yet verified at source)
model_mapping: twoway.py: state financing of schooling capacity -> s_t logit intercept; massabm params cost_jhs/cost_shs + cap_cost (state capacity multiplier)
confidence: medium-low (sign stable, SE large, identification weak)
test_experiment: raise the spending path 20% from t=10 in PH-like and KHM-like; predict +2pp secondary completion (0.111*ln(1.2)=+2.0%); falsified if completion moves <0.5pp

mechanism: same financing channel, but primary is already near-universal -> saturation
heterogeneity_country_type: SATURATED: only marginally positive where 1990 primary GER was high (+0.031*, 13 ctys); no effect in low-GER Asia (+0.049 ns)
literature_source: none needed; saturation is the finding
model_mapping: massabm: do NOT wire spending->primary completion; cap the level at the bar
test_experiment: in-model: double primary spend, expect <1pp GER change; if model moves >2pp the spending channel is mis-specified

mechanism: spending removes direct/opportunity cost of attendance
heterogeneity_country_type: no subgroup reaches significance; series definitions changed over time (UIS revisions)
model_mapping: massabm: idio_exit / exit hazard for Q1-Q2 households
test_experiment: would need a national EMIS series with a stable definition; blocked (see TARGETS_FLOW.csv unresolved rows)

mechanism: income raises the affordability of the college cost and the demand for the credential
heterogeneity_country_type: HOLDS STRONGLY in Asia (+1.075***, 19 ctys); FAILS outside Asia (+0.281 ns); not attenuated by income level (low 0.846***, high 0.697***)
model_mapping: twoway.py: g (income growth) and cost_col / feasible_share(cost_col, inc_sig) -> c_t; massabm y_median growth and borrow
test_experiment: raise g by 1pp/yr for 20y in PH-like; the model must produce ~+17% tertiary entry (0.85*ln(1.22)); falsified if <5%

mechanism: income growth loosens the household budget constraint at the secondary margin
method: two-way FE and first differences, CR1
identification_grade: correlational (FD is stronger: removes country trends)
heterogeneity_country_type: Asia +0.211**; non-Asia +0.166 ns; low-urban +0.141 vs high-urban +0.017
data_source: data/panel_results.csv spec S08, S08-FD; heterogeneity region/urb_grp
model_mapping: massabm growth / y_median; twoway g -> s_t via fea and cost
test_experiment: +1pp/yr growth in KHM-like for 15y -> +5-8pp secondary completion; check sign and rough magnitude

mechanism: income -> completion; also a mechanical link because completion is measured on the relevant-age cohort
heterogeneity_country_type: non-Asia +0.488** > Asia +0.350* (p=0.062); high-urban +0.446* vs low-urban +0.030 ns
model_mapping: massabm completion of diploma tier; twoway s_t
test_experiment: in-model income shock; compare completion response by country profile

mechanism: cohort size/fertility raises competition for fixed school resources and lowers per-child investment
identification_grade: plausibly-causal (mechanical resource-dilution channel + timing of fertility decline precedes cohort entry)
heterogeneity_country_type: HOLDS in both Asia (-0.172***) and non-Asia (-0.222***); strongest where 1990 completion was LOW (-0.171***) and in low-urban countries (-0.213***)
model_mapping: twoway births; massabm N/cohort size and per-child costs
test_experiment: lower births from 3.0 to 2.0 over 20y in PH-like; expect +7-10pp primary completion (-0.189*ln(3/2)=-7.7%); falsified if model shows <2pp

mechanism: urban residence lowers the distance/relevance cost of secondary school and raises the return to credentials
unit: semi-elasticity per percentage point of urban share
heterogeneity_country_type: low-urban +0.155 vs high-urban +0.039 (mechanical: less room to move)
model_mapping: massabm urban_path, q_urban, rural_cost; twoway has no explicit urban term (candidate addition)
test_experiment: shift urban_path 10pp forward; expect <1pp GER change in FE spec

mechanism: private providers add places the state does not finance (supply) rather than crowd out public enrolment
heterogeneity_country_type: HOLDS ONLY where state capacity/income is low: Asia +0.086***, non-Asia +0.003; low-income-1990 +0.081***, high-income +0.014 ns; low-tax-capacity +0.102***, high-tax-capacity -0.065 ns
model_mapping: twoway provider entry n_cm (e_cm, F_cm) and massabm private/agency channels
test_experiment: add a private-provider entry arm to twoway in KHM-like only; predict +7.5% GER per doubling of private share; falsified if PH-like (high private share) shows no capacity expansion

mechanism: teacher supply = realised school capacity; mechanically co-determined with enrolment
identification_grade: correlational (partly mechanical: teachers and pupils are the two terms of the pupil-teacher ratio)
heterogeneity_country_type: low-income-1990 +0.528*** vs high-income +0.192 ns; low-tax +0.510*** vs high-tax +0.244 ns -> binding supply constraint only in low-capacity states
data_source: data/panel_results.csv spec S18, S18-FD; heterogeneity income_grp/bursary_grp
model_mapping: massabm capacity (places) and twoway cap_cm/cap_tt; should enter as a capacity constraint, not a behavioural elasticity
confidence: medium (sign certain, magnitude inflated by mechanical co-movement)
test_experiment: do NOT calibrate; instead treat models supply-limited if teacher stock < N*ptr/35

mechanism: class size/quality channel: more teachers per pupil -> better learning -> completion
identification_grade: not identifiable (level and FD estimates have OPPOSITE signs: an enrolment boom raises PTR first and completion later)
heterogeneity_country_type: high-urban +0.547*** and high-income +0.579** in levels (the mechanical enrolment-boom pattern); low-urban/low-income insignificant
model_mapping: twoway quality channel (Qs/Qd dilution), massabm hc_school learning
confidence: low (sign conflict reported honestly, not resolved)
test_experiment: in-model, hold capacity fixed and raise intake: PTR rises then completion falls with a lag; require the model to reproduce the FD sign

mechanism: state capacity / fiscal space: education budgets are constrained by the tax take
heterogeneity_country_type: HOLDS in Asia (+0.541***) and low-urban (+0.582***) and low-GER countries (+0.431***); FAILS in non-Asia (-0.320 ns), high-urban (+0.169 ns), high-tax-capacity (+0.614*** but that is a select group)
data_source: data/panel_results.csv spec S24, S24-FD; heterogeneity region/urb_grp/base_ger
model_mapping: massabm state capacity K and tax_income (fiscal.py); twoway no state budget -> candidate addition
test_experiment: raise tax take 3pp in KHM-like; expect +1.2% education spend; check the fiscal ledger stays balanced

mechanism: education -> economy: human capital raises productivity (the model assumes eps_ec>=0)
unit: pp of growth per log point of GER 15y earlier
identification_grade: not identifiable as causal (reverse causality, graduate surplus, cohort composition); but it REJECTS eps_ec>0 in this specification
heterogeneity_country_type: Asia and non-Asia both negative; no subgroup shows the assumed positive elasticity
model_mapping: twoway eps_ec (REGIMES R1..R10) and d_ec; massabm graduate supply / employer floor
confidence: medium as a caution; low as a causal estimate
test_experiment: the model should be RUN with eps_ec in {0, 0.3, 0.6} and the fit to PH/KHM 2000-2024 completion-vs-formal-jobs must not favour 0.6; if it does, the FE estimate is the loser and that must be stated

mechanism: information/aspiration channel; also correlated with modern-sector demand
heterogeneity_country_type: not tested (no clean split; the digital divide is a level shifter absorbed by country FE)
model_mapping: not in either model (candidate for a demand shifter in twoway)
test_experiment: n/a until a demand-side shifter exists in twoway

mechanism: migration income relaxes household credit constraints for schooling
identification_grade: not identifiable at cross-country level (remittance series are small and volatile, and migration selection dominates)
heterogeneity_country_type: PHL-specific effects cannot be recovered from 30-country FE; needs a household survey
model_mapping: massabm remit_share / os_agency channel (consumption tax base)
test_experiment: blocked: needs FIES/APIS microdata (04_data/TARGETS_FLOW.csv marks PHL dropout/informality unresolved)

mechanism: child-labour opportunity cost: agrarian economies pull children out of school
heterogeneity_country_type: no significant split; the sign is wrong-signed for the simple opportunity-cost channel, plausibly because declining agriculture coincides with urban schooling expansion
model_mapping: massabm child_wage / farm option; do not wire this sign into the model
test_experiment: n/a as a parameter: the sign is contrary to the opportunity-cost story, so the model must NOT wire it; test only that the reported sign is reproduced by an auxiliary regression before any use

mechanism: vocational tracks are more costly and more selective -> dampen aggregate GER
unit: semi-elasticity per pp of vocational share
heterogeneity_country_type: not split (vocational share is available for too few country-years)
model_mapping: massabm vocational option / floorworld vocational share
test_experiment: minor: -1.5% GER per 10pp vocational share; test whether the model reproduces the sign

mechanism: the reform adds Grades 11-12 to the upper-secondary level; GER can jump mechanically
method: interrupted time series (linear pre-trend + post level shift)
identification_grade: plausibly-causal for the NULL: no level jump in total secondary GER
heterogeneity_country_type: PHL only; the K-12 "surge" is a composition/denominator effect, not a level shift
literature_source: COUNTRY_CARDS/PHL.md §5 policy timeline (primary documents NOT retrieved)
model_mapping: massabm K-12 rule (2016 switch) and twoway YEARS/Y_DIP/Y_COL
test_experiment: the in-model K-12 experiment must reproduce "no total-GER jump, upper-secondary level shift"; if it produces a total-GER surge, the accounting is wrong

mechanism: removing tuition should raise tertiary enrolment
identification_grade: correlational: confounded by the K-12 rollout (first SHS cohort entered tertiary only in 2018-19)
heterogeneity_country_type: PHL only
data_source: data/event_windows_gmr.csv PHL 2018 (and WDI spec in data/event_windows.csv)
model_mapping: massabm tuition_path (2017-2018 halving) and cost_col in twoway
confidence: medium that the event is confounded; the model must NOT treat free tuition as a positive shock without the K-12 confound
test_experiment: twoway arm with tuition cut + K-12 cohort delay; the model must show a dip then recovery, not an immediate jump

mechanism: legal compulsion raises enrolment
heterogeneity_country_type: CHN; the law was enforced province-by-province, so a national ITS understates it
model_mapping: massabm bar_basic / compulsory schooling rule
test_experiment: enforce a completion floor in the model at a calendar year; compare the implied GER jump to +32%

mechanism: positional competition: demand rises as the household approaches the high-stakes gate
identification_grade: correlational (cross-stage, same schools; not a panel)
heterogeneity_country_type: HKG only; the gradient is monotone in gate proximity, which is the model's R_gate channel
literature_source: Bray & Kwok (2003) Economics of Education Review 22:611-620, Table 1 p.616
model_mapping: twoway T_S/T_C: +0.7*log(R_S), +0.8*log(R_C) positional terms; massabm tut_cost/tut_effect
test_experiment: in twoway, move a cohort from S1-3 to S6-7 (raise R_gate 2x): the take-up must rise ~+35pp; if the positional coefficient delivers <10pp the gate channel is too weak

mechanism: tutoring is a normal/luxury good: spending rises faster than income
se_or_range: derived: 183k won (<3m) vs 671k won (>=8m); income gap 2.67x -> spend gap 3.67x
heterogeneity_country_type: KOR (high-income, high-gate); not transferable to KHM/PHL without a survey
literature_source: MODS/KEDI Private Education Expenditures Survey 2023 (English release), Table 2 + income table
model_mapping: twoway T_S/T_C demand (income enters via feasible_share/inc_sig); massabm y_sigma and tut_cost
test_experiment: in twoway, widen inc_sig: the top-quintile spend share must rise super-proportionally (elasticity ~1.3)

mechanism: participation falls with level (voluntary/less time) while spend per student rises (gate price)
heterogeneity_country_type: KOR; contradicts the naive "participation rises with gate proximity" if taken alone - the intensive margin (price) rises where the extensive margin falls
model_mapping: twoway: separate T_S (extensive) and quality/price margin, or a two-margin tutoring block
test_experiment: require the model to produce falling participation and rising spend at the college gate simultaneously; a one-margin model cannot

mechanism: urban density lowers the cost of finding a tutor and raises peer competition
estimate: Japan 57.9% (Tokyo) vs 22.1% (Akita) = 2.62x; Cambodia grade-6 60.5% urban vs 26.4% rural = 2.29x
se_or_range: JPN: prefecture table; KHM: 6-school case study (NOT national)
heterogeneity_country_type: holds in both a rich (KOR/JPN) and a poor (KHM) setting in sign; magnitude unverified in KHM
literature_source: Rappleye & Komatsu (2020) EPAA 28(67) Table 2; Brehm & Silova (2013/2014)
model_mapping: massabm urban_path and q_urban in the tutoring decision; twoway has no urban term (candidate addition)
test_experiment: add an urban gradient to twoway T_S; require 2x urban/rural take-up ratio

mechanism: regulatory suppression of the commercial academic-tutoring market
se_or_range: 2014: peer-reviewed abstract, survey table not retrieved; 2022: newspaper headline only (LOW)
identification_grade: not identifiable (no common survey instrument; the 2022 figure is a bound from a headline)
heterogeneity_country_type: CHN only; the political-economy shock has no analogue in PHL/KHM/HKG
literature_source: Liu & Bray (2020) Educational Studies 46(2):170-187 (ERIC EJ1245506); China Education Daily 2022-03-03
model_mapping: massabm/twoway shadow-sector supply shock (F_cm up / forbidden segment)
test_experiment: shock n_cm to near zero from t=2021 and watch for a substitution into teacher-tutoring (n_tt) - the model predicts rerouting, data cannot yet confirm it

mechanism: higher returns raise the payoff to positional investment
estimate: NOT ESTIMABLE at cross-country level: 4 observed countries (PHL/KHM/CHN/HKG), 3 shadow survey years
method: cannot run; fewer than 5 country-year cells and no common instrument
heterogeneity_country_type: the pattern (HK 70% at the senior gate, KHM 60% urban) is consistent with returns/gate intensity but cannot separate the two
literature_source: Bray & Kwok 2003; Brehm & Silova 2014; Liu & Bray 2020; Abarcar & Theoharides 2024 (Mincer returns not verified)
model_mapping: twoway T_S: +0.9*log1p(ret_S) - the coefficient the model needs and the data cannot supply
test_experiment: mark as P4-pending: needs a household survey with both tutoring and earnings; the in-model coefficient must stay a prior (0.9), not an estimate

mechanism: legal compulsion raises enrolment
estimate: NOT ESTIMATED: the observed 6-country GMR panel has <13 usable observations per country-event window (secondary GER series are sparse before 1998 for HKG/KOR/KHM)
method: blocked (insufficient observed cells; never impute the gap)
identification_grade: not identifiable with the data on disk
model_mapping: massabm bar_basic
test_experiment: blocked: needs national GER series pre-1998 (EDB tables cover HK; KEDI covers KOR) - pull and rerun

mechanism: expected migration raises the return to the licensed credential -> more people sit and pass licensure
estimate: 9.0 licensed nurses per additional nurse migrant; +3.9 nurses per 100k (126% of pre-mean 3.1)
heterogeneity_country_type: PHL; requires an overseas professional channel that KHM/CHN lack
literature_source: Abarcar & Theoharides (2024), as compiled in ECON_TARGETS (FULL-TEXT per ECON_LIT)
model_mapping: massabm os_prof vacancy/pool chain and board-exam supply; the model currently fails this (0.25 vs 9)
test_experiment: the existing massabm nurse_check: the model must produce ~9 licensed per migrant; currently 0.25 - the gap is the finding

mechanism: price suppresses take-up
estimate: NOT IDENTIFIED: no credible price elasticity located in ECON_TARGETS (row 23 = unusable); twoway uses -1.1 on p/ret as a declared prior
model_mapping: twoway T_S/T_C price term (currently a prior, not an estimate)
test_experiment: sensitivity: run twoway price coefficient in {-1.1, -0.5, -2.0}; report which arms survive

mechanism: physical access: a school within walking distance raises enrolment, especially for girls
estimate: NOT VERIFIED AT SOURCE THIS SESSION: the canonical Indonesian INPRES estimate (Duflo 2001) is cited in the literature as ~+0.12-0.19 years of schooling per school built, but the original was not retrieved
identification_grade: causal in the original (policy discontinuity); not verified here
heterogeneity_country_type: low-enrolment, low-income rural settings; likely no effect at near-universal enrolment (matches R02)
literature_source: Duflo (2001) AER 91(4) - CITED BUT NOT RETRIEVED THIS SESSION; must be checked before use
model_mapping: massabm capacity/places and rural_cost
test_experiment: build schools in the model at t=5 in KHM-like; expect +0.1-0.2 years of schooling; falsified if <0.05
